Add a build-level check that fails when two compiled orca classes have names differing only in letter case, and fix two stale references in AGENTS.md. This replaces PR https://github.com/VirtusLab/orca/pull/263 (which did the check as a munit test in the shell module).

## Why

On a case-insensitive filesystem (macOS default), two class files whose names differ only in case (e.g. `orca/Stage$package.class` and `orca/stage$package.class`) make the JVM load the wrong file and fail with `NoClassDefFoundError`. This happened before (#190, fixed by renames in #198 and #200). Linux CI never hits it, so the check must compare names, not touch the filesystem.

## 1. sbt task `checkClassNameCase`

- Define a `taskKey[Unit]` named `checkClassNameCase` and set it on the `orcaRoot` project in `build.sbt`. If the body is more than a few lines, put the logic in a new file under `project/` (e.g. `project/ClassNameCase.scala`, like the existing `project/ConcatDocs.scala`) and keep only the key and its wiring in `build.sbt`.
- Scope: every project aggregated by `orcaRoot` (not the root itself), both `Compile` and `Test` configurations. Use a `ScopeFilter(inAggregates(ThisProject, includeRoot = false), inConfigurations(Compile, Test))`.
- First make sure everything is compiled (`compile.all(filter).value`), then collect all `*.class` files under every `classDirectory.all(filter).value`, as paths relative to their class directory (e.g. `orca/stage$package.class`). Deduplicate.
- Group by lower-cased path; any group with more than one distinct name is a collision. If there are collisions, fail the task (`sys.error`) with a message listing each colliding group (sorted, e.g. `orca/Stage$package.class vs orca/stage$package.class`), and saying they break on case-insensitive filesystems.
- Example sketch (adjust as needed, must compile):

```scala
lazy val checkClassNameCase =
  taskKey[Unit]("Fails if two compiled orca classes differ only in letter case")

checkClassNameCase := {
  val scopes = ScopeFilter(inAggregates(ThisProject, includeRoot = false), inConfigurations(Compile, Test))
  val _ = compile.all(scopes).value
  val names = classDirectory.all(scopes).value.flatMap { dir =>
    (dir ** "*.class").get.flatMap(IO.relativize(dir, _))
  }.distinct
  val collisions = names.groupBy(_.toLowerCase).values.filter(_.size > 1).map(_.sorted.mkString(" vs "))
  if (collisions.nonEmpty)
    sys.error(s"Class names differing only in case (break on case-insensitive filesystems):\n${collisions.mkString("\n")}")
}
```

## 2. Run it in CI

In `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, the `test` job runs `sbt +test`. Change it to also run the new task in the same sbt invocation: `sbt +test checkClassNameCase`.

## 3. AGENTS.md fixes

`recordAndCommit` and `resumeFrom` now live in `flow/src/main/scala/orca/stage.scala`, not in `Flow`. In AGENTS.md:
- in the capability-gating section, replace "`Flow`'s\n  `recordAndCommit`" with "`stage.scala`'s\n  `recordAndCommit`" (keep the line wrapping);
- in the storage table row for `.orca/runs/<key>.progress.json`, replace `Flow.recordAndCommit` with `` `stage.scala`'s `recordAndCommit` `` and `Flow.resumeFrom` with `` `stage.scala`'s `resumeFrom` ``.
Do not touch files under `docs/plans/` or `docs/research/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- `sbt checkClassNameCase` passes on the current code.
- Verify it fails: temporarily add a file `shell/src/test/scala/orca/Stage.scala` containing a top-level def (e.g. `def probe(): Int = 1`), run `sbt checkClassNameCase`, confirm it fails naming `orca/Stage$package.class` vs `orca/stage$package.class`, then delete the probe file. Do not commit the probe.
- No new compiler warnings; `sbt scalafmtCheckAll` clean.
- Keep comments minimal: one short comment on the task saying why names are compared (Linux CI can't hit the filesystem collision).
- PR description: short and simple; say it supersedes #263 and credits its author (@lukaszlenart) for the original idea and the AGENTS.md fix.

resultJson.title: Add build-level class name case collision check
resultJson.body:
Add a build-level check that fails when two compiled orca classes have names differing only in letter case. This prevents silent class-loading failures on case-insensitive filesystems (macOS), where such files overwrite each other and the JVM loads the wrong one.

The check compares class file paths (not filesystem behavior), making it reliable on Linux CI where case-insensitivity never occurs in practice but collisions still break on developer machines and macOS CI.

Also fix two stale references in AGENTS.md: `recordAndCommit` and `resumeFrom` now live in `stage.scala`, not `Flow`.

This supersedes #263. Thanks to @lukaszlenart for the original idea and the documentation fix.
